summary: The submission investigates the impact of reference activation width on delayed recall and sequential board-editing tasks in feed-forward networks. While increasing the reference width from 4 to 32 slots solves information bottleneck constraints in a delayed recall task (reaching ~99.9% accuracy), the models still fail to outperform a trivial 50% baseline on board editing due to optimization and editing execution challenges.
strengths: Precise specification of experimental setups, hyperparameters, learning rates, loss weightings, and model layer dimensions.
Well-structured pre-specified validation rules and clear reporting of negative/null results where models failed to surpass simple copy heuristics.
Thoughtful isolation of memory capacity vs. operational update capability via the Experiment 2 diagnostic bottleneck.
weaknesses: Under the review criteria for external reproducibility, the submission is categorized as text-only without a verified, functional open-source codebase checked into Pubroot's registry.
Optimization dynamics degrade significantly between epoch 4 and epoch 16, indicating overfitting or optimization instability that limits generalizability.
Evaluation is confined to three seeds on a narrow synthetic task distribution.
suggestions: Explore learning rate decay schedules, regularization, or alternative optimizers to prevent the performance drop observed between epochs 4 and 16.
Expand the task setup to evaluate partial/selective board updates where keeping a fixed reference vs. mutable slots provides distinct functional trade-offs.

claims.text: DenseNet connects each layer to every other layer in a feed-forward fashion, reusing features from earlier layers.
Each of 16 squares starts with one of eight colors. The original board has 48 bits of entropy before the query position is known.
claims.source: Mathematical calculation: 16 squares * log2(8) = 16 * 3 = 48 bits of entropy.

claims.text: A linear encoder maps the 128 concatenated one-hot inputs to 256 values.
claims.source: Architectural dimension calculation: 16 squares * 8 one-hot classes = 128 input dimensions mapped to 256 hidden dimension.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Densely Connected Convolutional Networks
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies explicit read-only activation channel reservation to investigate memory retention vs. active state manipulation in sequential editing tasks, contrasting with standard dense feature concatenation across CNN layers.
